content.text: <user_input mode="act"># Delphi Sticky Note Application — Comprehensive Codebase AnalysisYou are acting as a **senior Delphi architect and codebase auditor**.I have an existing **Sticky Note application built with Delphi**. You may run safe commands needed to inspect the project and, if appropriate, compile/test it without modifying source files.8. Do not assume how the application works. Inspect the actual code.9. Every important conclusion must be supported by evidence from the repository.10. If something cannot be determined, explicitly mark it as **Unknown / Not Verified**.11. Preserve the current application as-is.---# 1. Repository DiscoveryFirst inspect the complete repository structure.Identify:* Delphi project files (`.dpr`, `.dproj`, `.groupproj`)* Forms (`.pas`, `.dfm`)* Data modules* Units* Resources* Images/icons* Configuration files* Database files* SQL scripts* Components* Third-party libraries* Packages* Tests* Documentation* Build scripts* Installer/deployment filesDetermine:* Delphi version/compiler version if detectable* Target platforms* Win32 / Win64 support* VCL or FMX* Application entry point* Main form* Major modules* External dependenciesCreate a high-level architecture map.---# 2. Application Purpose & Feature InventoryDetermine exactly what the Sticky Note application currently does.Identify all implemented functionality, including but not limited to:* Create note* Edit note* Delete note* Duplicate note* Move note* Resize note* Minimize/restore note* Pin/always-on-top* Change note color* Change font* Rich text/plain text* Search* Categories/tags* Archive* Trash* Favorites* Reminders* Notifications* Auto-save* Manual save* Note persistence* Startup behavior* Tray icon* Global hotkeys* Keyboard shortcuts* Drag & drop* Copy/paste* Undo/redo* Context menus* Multi-note support* Multi-monitor behavior* Position persistence* Window size persistence* Settings/preferences* Import/export* Backup/restore* Printing* Synchronization* Encryption/security* Database supportDo not assume features exist merely because there is UI code for them. Verify their implementation.Produce a feature matrix:| Feature | Exists | Fully Implemented | Partially Implemented | Evidence || ------- | ------ | ----------------- | --------------------- | -------- |---# 3. User Interface AnalysisAnalyze every form and visual component.For each form identify:* Purpose* Main controls* Events* Data sources* User interactions* Menus* Toolbars* Context menus* Keyboard shortcuts* Dialogs* Custom painting* Custom controls* Windows API usageEvaluate the UI architecture.Look for:* Absolute positioning* Hard-coded dimensions* Hard-coded colors* Hard-coded fonts* DPI problems* High-DPI awareness* Scaling issues* Multi-monitor issues* Dark mode support* Theme support* Accessibility* Keyboard navigation* RTL/localization considerations* Modern Windows compatibilityIdentify visual inconsistencies and usability problems.---# 4. Delphi Architecture AnalysisAnalyze the code architecture in detail.Determine whether the application follows:* Monolithic form architecture* Separation of concerns* MVC* MVP* MVVM* Service-oriented architecture* Repository pattern* Data module architecture* Other patternsAnalyze dependencies between:* Forms* Business logic* Data access* Models* Services* Utility units* Windows API wrappersIdentify violations such as:* Business logic inside forms* SQL inside UI event handlers* Global variables* Global state* Singleton abuse* Tight coupling* Circular dependencies* God objects/forms* Excessive `uses` dependencies* Hidden side effectsProvide a dependency overview.---# 5. Code Quality ReviewReview the Delphi code for:* Naming conventions* Code organization* Method size* Class responsibilities* Duplication* Dead code* Comment quality* Exception handling* Resource management* Object ownership* Memory management* Interface/reference counting* String handling* Variant usage* Pointer usage* Windows API handling* Thread safety* Global state* Constants/enums* Magic numbers* Magic stringsPay particular attention to Delphi-specific risks:* Object lifetime bugs* Double-free risks* Ownership problems* `Free` vs `FreeAndNil`* Interface/object lifetime interactions* Dataset lifetime* FireDAC resource handling* String encoding* Unicode compatibility* `TThread` usage* Synchronization* Anonymous methods* Event handler lifetime* Component ownershipClassify findings as:* 🔴 Critical* 🟠 High* 🟡 Medium* 🟢 Low---# 6. Data Persistence AnalysisDetermine how notes are stored.Possible mechanisms include:* INI* JSON* XML* SQLite* Firebird* Registry* Files* Embedded database* Windows settings* Custom binary formatAnalyze:* Data model* Schema* Serialization* Deserialization* Versioning* Migration* Corruption handling* Backup* Recovery* Atomic writes* Concurrent access* File locking* Data validationIf a database exists, document:* Tables* Fields* Primary keys* Foreign keys* Indexes* Constraints* RelationshipsProduce a logical data model.---# 7. Windows IntegrationBecause this is a desktop Sticky Note application, inspect Windows-specific behavior carefully.Identify use of:* WinAPI* Shell API* Registry* Windows messages* Hooks* Hotkeys* Taskbar* Notification area/system tray* Jump lists* Notifications* Startup registration* File associations* Clipboard* Drag/drop* Always-on-top* Layered windows* Transparency* Aero/DWM* Multi-monitor APIs* DPI APIs* Power/session eventsDocument all Windows-specific dependencies.Determine whether the application behaves correctly on modern Windows 10/11.---# 8. Persistence & Crash SafetyAnalyze what happens when:* Application closes normally* Windows shuts down* Application crashes* PC loses power* Note is edited but not explicitly saved* Multiple notes are edited simultaneously* Storage becomes unavailable* Stored data becomes corruptedDetermine whether autosave exists.If autosave exists, document:* Trigger* Frequency/debounce* Implementation* Failure handlingAssess whether data loss is possible.---# 9. Performance AnalysisIdentify possible performance bottlenecks.Look for:* Heavy work on UI thread* Excessive disk I/O* Excessive database queries* Repeated serialization* Large loops* Memory leaks* Resource leaks* Excessive form creation* Excessive repainting* Timer abuse* Background thread issuesEstimate scalability:* 10 notes* 100 notes* 1,000 notes* 10,000 notesIdentify likely bottlenecks.---# 10. Security & PrivacyAnalyze:* Local data exposure* Sensitive information storage* Plain-text notes* Encryption* Password protection* Temporary files* Logs* Clipboard exposure* Registry storage* Network communication* External services* Update mechanismsIdentify realistic security/privacy risks.Do not invent threats that are not applicable.---# 11. Error HandlingInspect exception handling throughout the application.Identify:* Empty `except` blocks* Broad exception swallowing* Missing validation* Unhandled exceptions* User-unfriendly errors* Logging* Recovery mechanisms* Data corruption handlingDetermine whether failures are:* Recoverable* Fatal* Silent* User-visible---# 12. Testing & Build QualityDetermine whether automated tests exist.Identify:* DUnitX* DUnit* Integration tests* UI tests* Database tests* Smoke testsDetermine:* Number of tests* Coverage if available* What is tested* What is not tested* Build reproducibility* Compiler warnings* Static analysisIf safe, run the existing test suite and report the result.Do NOT modify tests.---# 13. Third-Party Components & DependenciesInventory every external dependency.For each:| Dependency | Purpose | Version | Open Source/Commercial | Required? | Risk || ---------- | ------- | ------- | ---------------------- | --------- | ---- |Identify:* Abandoned libraries* Outdated libraries* Components incompatible with modern Delphi* Components with licensing concerns* Components that could be replaced with native Delphi functionality---# 14. Technical DebtCreate a technical debt inventory.For every significant issue:| ID | Problem | Location | Severity | Impact | Recommended Direction || -- | ------- | -------- | -------- | ------ | --------------------- |Separate:### Critical technical debtThings that can cause data loss, crashes, corruption, or inability to build.### Architectural debtProblems that make future development difficult.### Maintainability debtProblems that increase development cost.### UI/UX debtProblems affecting usability.### Compatibility debtProblems affecting modern Windows/Delphi versions.---# 15. Architecture DiagramCreate a text-based architecture diagram such as:Application│├── UI│   ├── Main Form│   ├── Note Form│   └── Settings│├── Application Services│├── Domain/Models│├── Persistence│└── Windows IntegrationUse the actual architecture discovered in the repository.Do not invent layers that don't exist.---# 16. Current Architecture AssessmentGive the application an overall architecture score from 1–10.Score separately:* Architecture* Maintainability* Code quality* UI/UX* Reliability* Performance* Security* Testing* Windows integration* ExtensibilityExplain every score briefly.---# 17. Modernization AssessmentAssume the long-term goal is to make this a **modern, stable, maintainable Delphi Sticky Note application**.Identify what should be:### KEEPExisting implementation that is sound.### IMPROVEExisting implementation that can be incrementally improved.### REFACTORCode that should be structurally reorganized.### REPLACETechnology/components/architecture that should be replaced.### REMOVEUnused, obsolete, or unnecessary functionality.Do not implement anything yet.---# 18. Recommended Target ArchitectureDesign a proposed target architecture suitable for modern Delphi.Consider separation into:* Presentation/UI* Application services* Domain/model* Persistence* Infrastructure* Windows integration* Configuration* Logging* TestingBut only recommend layers that provide real value for this application.The target architecture should remain pragmatic rather than over-engineered.---# 19. Modern Feature OpportunitiesAfter understanding the existing application, identify useful modern features that could improve it.Consider:* Modern Windows 11 UI* Dark/light themes* High-DPI support* Better note search* Tags* Pinning* Note grouping* Rich text* Markdown* Attachments* Images* Checklists* Reminders* Notifications* Global hotkeys* System tray* Multiple monitors* Cloud sync* Local backup* Import/export* Encryption* Search indexing* Templates* Archive/trash* Keyboard-first workflowClearly separate:**Currently implemented**from**Recommended future features**.---# 20. Migration StrategyCreate a safe modernization roadmap.Use phases such as:### Phase 0 — BaselineDocument current behavior and establish a clean build/test baseline.### Phase 1 — ReliabilityFix crashes, persistence problems, resource leaks, and data-loss risks.### Phase 2 — ArchitectureSeparate UI, application logic, domain logic, and persistence.### Phase 3 — Data LayerImprove persistence, versioning, backup, and recovery.### Phase 4 — UI/UXModernize the visual experience and improve DPI/theme/multi-monitor support.### Phase 5 — Windows IntegrationImprove tray, notifications, hotkeys, startup, and Windows 11 integration.### Phase 6 — Search & OrganizationImprove search, tags, categories, archive, etc.### Phase 7 — Advanced FeaturesOnly after the foundation is stable.### Phase 8 — Testing & ReleaseAutomated regression testing, installer, versioning, diagnostics, and release process.Adjust these phases based on what you actually discover.---# 21. Prioritized RecommendationsProduce a final prioritized backlog.Use:| Priority | ID | Recommendation | Reason | Risk | Effort || -------- | -- | -------------- | ------ | ---- | ------ |Priorities:* P0 — Must fix* P1 — High value* P2 — Important* P3 — Nice to have---# 22. Final Executive ReportFinish with a concise executive summary containing:## Application OverviewWhat the application is and how it currently works.## Current ArchitectureHow the code is organized today.## Biggest StrengthsTop 5 strengths.## Biggest ProblemsTop 10 problems, ranked by severity.## Biggest RisksData-loss, stability, maintainability, compatibility, security, etc.## Modernization OpportunitiesTop 10 improvements.## Recommended Target ArchitectureShort description and diagram.## Recommended RoadmapOrdered implementation phases.## Estimated ComplexityClassify the modernization as:* Small* Medium* Large* Very LargeExplain why.## Overall AssessmentGive a final score from 1–10 and explain it.---# IMPORTANT: OUTPUT FORMATDo NOT modify the repository.Produce a report named:`STICKY_NOTE_APPLICATION_ANALYSIS.md`However, **do not create the file**. 1 | # Sticky Notes
  2 | 
  3 | A lightweight desktop sticky notes application for Windows, built with Delphi using a clean, modular architecture.
  4 | 
  5 | ## Features
  6 | 
  7 | - **Colorful sticky notes** - 8 colors (Yellow, Green, Blue, Pink, Purple, Orange, White, Gray)
  8 | - **Native window behavior** - Drag from header, resize from edges using Windows WM_NCHITTEST
  9 | - **Always on Top** - Keep notes visible above other windows
 10 | - **Collapse** - Minimize to header only
 11 | - **Lock** - Prevent accidental edits
 12 | - **Global hotkeys** - `Ctrl+Alt+N` for new note, `Ctrl+Alt+F` for search
 13 | - **Auto-save** - Debounced save (1 second default) on typing, moving, resizing
 14 | - **Light/Dark theme** - Windows 10 / Windows 10 Dark styles
 15 | - **Auto-start** - Launch with Windows
 16 | - **Backup & Restore** - ZIP-based backups
 17 | - **Multi-monitor support** - Notes stay on their monitor
 18 | - **JSON storage** - One file per note, easy to sync with Git/Dropbox/OneDrive
 19 | 
 20 | ## Architecture
 21 | 
 22 | Clean separation of concerns:
 23 | 
 24 | ```
 25 | Forms/          # UI only (Views)
 26 | Controllers/    # Business logic (NoteManager, TrayController, SettingsController)
 27 | Models/         # Data (Note, Settings, Enums)
 28 | Storage/        # Abstract persistence (JSON, SQLite stub)
 29 | Services/       # Cross-cutting (Autosave, Hotkeys, Theme, Backup, Startup)
 30 | Utils/          # Shared helpers (Window, JSON, Color, Monitor)
 31 | ```
 32 | 
 33 | See [docs/ARCHITECTURE.md](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md) for detailed documentation.
 34 | 
 35 | ## Building
 36 | 
 37 | ### Requirements
 38 | - Delphi 11 Alexandria or later
 39 | - Windows 10/11
 40 |

 42 | 1. Open `src/StickyNotes.dproj`
 43 | 2. Build (Ctrl+F9) or Run (F9)
 44 | 
 45 | ### Command Line
 46 | ```bash
 47 | msbuild src/StickyNotes.dproj /p:Config=Release /p:Platform=Win32
 48 | ```
 49 |

 51 |

 53 | 
 54 | ```
 55 | %APPDATA%\StickyNotes\
 56 | ├── settings.ini
 57 | └── notes\
 58 |     ├── 0000000001.json
 59 |     └── ...
 60 | ```
 61 |
